name: Glutathione injections
lead: Glutathione (GSH) is a small tripeptide made of glutamate, cysteine and glycine that cells produce naturally and use as a major antioxidant.[1] Intravenous or intramuscular glutathione is promoted in some countries and online communities as a skin-lightening treatment, often alongside vitamin C.[2]

Reference works state that whether glutathione actually lightens skin was unclear as of 2019, citing a systematic review, and that the Philippine government recommends against intravenous glutathione because of possible side effects.[2] No controlled clinical trial of injected glutathione for general skin lightening was found among the study records reviewed for this article.

paras: Glutathione is built from glutamate, cysteine and glycine, with cysteine joined through an unusual gamma linkage that helps resist peptide breakdown. In healthy cells more than 90 percent of the pool is in the reduced form, and intracellular concentrations are far higher than extracellular ones.[1]

It neutralises reactive oxygen species, supports enzymes such as glutathione peroxidases, helps keep vitamins C and E in their active forms, and conjugates reactive metabolites such as the toxic acetaminophen metabolite NAPQI.[1] The reference article notes that oral glutathione is poorly absorbed systemically, because digestive proteases break it down.[1]

Glutathione is described as the most common agent taken by mouth to lighten skin, and it is also used in creams.[2] Proponents of injection say it bypasses the poor oral absorption and reduces melanin production. The text of this article reports only what the sources state: that the proposed mechanism is not established by trials found here, and the encyclopedia record calls effectiveness unclear.[2]

No studies found of injected glutathione for general skin lightening. One registered trial (NCT07595705) is testing a vitamin C and glutathione approach for gingival hyperpigmentation, which concerns gum tissue and is not a study of skin lightening; it is recruiting.[3] A trial of a multi-ingredient injectable (NCT07929870) listing skin pigmentation among its outcomes has not started recruiting.[4]
Related research includes animal studies of glutathione injection, for example in mice exposed to radiation and in rats with peritonitis, which are not studies of appearance.[5][6]
The Philippine government has recommended against intravenous glutathione because of possible side effects.[2] No controlled safety data for cosmetic injection use were found.

card.summary: Injected glutathione is used for skin lightening, but its effectiveness is unclear and the Philippine government advises against IV use.
card.note: Philippine government recommends against intravenous glutathione; efficacy unclear as of a 2019 review.

quick.overview:
Glutathione is an antioxidant peptide the body makes. Some clinics and online communities use injections or IV drips of it to lighten skin.

Reference works describe its effectiveness for skin whitening as unclear as of 2019. No controlled trial of injected glutathione for general skin lightening was found.
quick.mechanism: Proponents say glutathione reduces melanin production, and that injection avoids poor oral absorption. Reference sources confirm oral absorption is poor but do not establish the lightening mechanism.
quick.risks: The Philippine government recommends against intravenous glutathione because of possible side effects. No controlled safety data for cosmetic injection were found.
